This dehumidifies the air but leaves it in an overcooled state for temperature control. Both the CC and CRC coils employ a counterflow configuration for maximum effectiveness, and the CC outlet water temperature is greater than the CRC entering air temperature. The CRC therefore uses the warmed-up return water from the CC outlet at 64.5 °F to reheat the air. The chilled water is cooled back to 59.3 °F (CRC_outlet) while flowing through the CRC, while the outlet air from the cooling coil is reheated from 53.68 °F to 61.3 °F (CRC DA-T). The normal HEDS operation is similar to a variable air volume (VAV) HVAC system with the addition of the recovery coil and optimized control strategies described below. The proprietary control system is designed to control the HVAC operating parameters to maintain temperature and humidity within specified levels while minimizing energy consumption and maximizing occupant comfort. 1.1 Controls and Optimization of the HEDS Operation To significantly increase annual HVAC system savings, the HEDS unit is equipped with a factory installed, tested and commissioned HVAC optimization software package that resets the HVAC system setpoints to minimize energy use and promote stable and occupant friendly operation. The setpoints being reset include the following: • supply air dry bulb temperature, • supply air dewpoint temperature, • supply air static pressure, • chilled water supply temperature, • chilled water distribution loop differential pressure, • hot water supply temperature, • hot water distribution loop differential pressure. The HEDS HVAC system optimization software package continually evaluates the conditions at the loads and determines whether the loads are increasing or decreasing, evaluates the distance between the actual conditions and the desired conditions and how long the controlled variables have been away from their desired conditions, and then creates small changes in the setpoints, with updates taking place every minute. As a variable moves further away from its desired value, the changes are larger, as the variable gets closer to its desired value, the changes are smaller. As a part of the HEDS HVAC optimization software, there is functionality for “Thermal Flywheel” operation that contributes to significant chiller and boiler system runtime reductions. The Thermal Flywheel software evaluates current conditions and those experienced during the previous day to determine whether it is possible to shut the boiler or chiller systems off and use stored energy in the building to “float” through a period, by allowing a slightly larger deviation from the desired conditions for a short period of time.
